properties.natural_language: The blockHash parameter in a filter request must be a valid 32-byte hex string.
The blockHash parameter must not be used together with fromBlock or toBlock parameters (mutual exclusivity).
The filter options must contain valid DATA-FILTER-OPTIONS and DATA-BLOCK-HASH fields with correct types.
The blockHash must reference a canonical chain block; uncle block hashes must be treated as not found.
When blockHash and fromBlock/toBlock are both specified, the request must always be rejected with an error, regardless of parameter values.
The node's block database must be complete and consistent such that block hash lookups return deterministic results.
Clients must not assume block hash query results are stable across chain reorganizations.
Block hash lookup operations must complete within bounded time to prevent denial of service from high query volume.
When a block is not found by hash, the error response must use code -32000 and include the requested block hash in the data field.
When a block is found, the returned logs must match the specified address and topics filter criteria.
After validation, if blockHash is present and no range parameters conflict, the hash format must be verified as valid 32-byte hex before proceeding to block lookup.
The error object must contain exactly three fields: code (-32000), message ('Block not found.'), and data (the requested block hash).
EOF bytecode submitted for deployment must begin with a valid EOF magic number and version header.
The EOF container must have structurally valid header sections before metadata parsing begins.
The metadata marker (0x05) must be correctly identified during header parsing; unrecognized section types must cause rejection.
The metadata_size field must be in the range 1 to 65535 (valid 16-bit unsigned integer, zero is invalid).
The metadata section must be positioned before the data section in the EOF container body.
An EOF container with invalid metadata size or incorrect section ordering must be rejected and cannot be deployed.
Metadata content encoding is opaque to the protocol; no protocol-level validation is performed on metadata bytes.
Verification tools consuming metadata must handle multiple encoding formats (CBOR, etc.) and gracefully handle malformed content.
Metadata content must not affect contract execution behavior; it is strictly non-executable auxiliary data.
Metadata claiming specific compiler versions or source hashes cannot be trusted without independent verification against recompiled bytecode.
After bytecode comparison, a contract is verified only if the recompiled bytecode (excluding metadata) matches the deployed bytecode exactly.
A received block must have sequential block number (parent_number + 1), valid timestamp ordering, and correct parent hash.
Block gas limit must be within parent_gas_limit +/- (parent_gas_limit / 1024) and must be >= 5000.
Ommer blocks must satisfy: at most 2, no duplicates, age between 1 and 6 blocks, valid ancestry, and not in canonical chain.
After block body application, the computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must all match the header values.
The block reward must be exactly 3 ETH for the miner, plus (3 ETH / 32) per included ommer.
Each ommer miner must receive exactly ((8 - ommer_age) * 3 ETH) / 8.
Before transaction execution: sender nonce must match, balance >= gas*price + value, sender must be EOA, and intrinsic gas must be met.
Gas refund must be capped at 50% of gas consumed during transaction execution.
Total gas accounting must be conserved: gas_charged_upfront = gas_refunded_to_sender + gas_paid_to_miner.
PoW result must satisfy: result_as_uint <= 2^256 / difficulty.
Difficulty calculation must correctly subtract BOMB_DELAY_BLOCKS (3,000,000) from block number before computing the bomb component.
The difficulty adjustment multiplier must be 2 when the parent block has ommers, and 1 otherwise.
The bomb component is 2^((block_number - 3000000) // 100000 - 2) and is only added when the exponent is non-negative.
Empty account cleanup at end of transaction must not delete accounts that have non-zero balance or non-empty code.
The 50% refund cap must prevent any transaction from receiving more gas refund than half of what it consumed.
ECDSA signature recovery must yield a valid sender address that corresponds to an externally owned account.
Log filter query parameters (address and topics) must be validated before bloom filter matching.
Query bloom positions must be computed using keccak256 hashing with correct 11-bit extraction (mask 0x07FF) from byte pairs.
Resource limits must be enforced on bloom filter searches to prevent unbounded log scanning from crafted queries.
Each bloom entry must set exactly 3 bits derived from the first 6 bytes of the keccak256 hash, using big-endian 11-bit extraction.
The bloom filter must be exactly 256 bytes (2048 bits) and initialized to all zeros before any entries are added.
If a block's bloom filter is missing any required query bits, the block definitively cannot contain matching logs.
If a block's bloom filter contains all required query bits, the block may contain matching logs (false positives possible).
The completed bloom filter must contain the bit patterns for all log addresses and all topics from the processed logs.
Bit position extraction uses big-endian byte ordering: hash[0]*256 + hash[1] masked with 0x07FF for the first position.
Log entries added to bloom filters must contain valid 20-byte addresses and 32-byte topics.
The 2048-bit bloom filter must remain effective (not saturated) for the expected number of log entries per block.
A transaction triggering SELFDESTRUCT must be a valid signed transaction with sufficient gas for execution.
The beneficiary address specified in SELFDESTRUCT must be a valid 20-byte Ethereum address.
After SELFDESTRUCT execution, the contract's entire ETH balance must be transferred to the specified beneficiary address.
After SELFDESTRUCT, the contract must be marked for destruction and its code and storage removed at end of transaction.
SELFDESTRUCT is deprecated (EIP-6049). Current semantics are valid but may change in future forks. New contracts must not rely on SELFDESTRUCT behavior.
Future breaking changes to SELFDESTRUCT must be communicated with sufficient advance notice before activation.
Alternative patterns must exist for legitimate use cases currently relying on SELFDESTRUCT before it is removed.
A beacon block received via gossip must have valid proposer index, BLS signature, and slot timing before acceptance.
In Gloas fork, beacon block gossip validation must replace execution payload checks with bid-based validation.
An execution payload bid must verify: builder is active (is_active_builder), payment > 0, fee_recipient and gas_limit match proposer preferences, and builder can cover bid (can_builder_cover_bid).
The builder's BLS signature on the execution payload bid must be cryptographically valid.
An execution payload envelope must have valid builder BLS signature, block root matching a known block, and payload matching the bid.
KZG commitments relocated to the bid message must be correctly validated for data column sidecars.
Proposer preferences must be validated: proposer is assigned to declared slot in next epoch, BLS signature is valid, and preferences are well-formed.
Sync responses must match request parameters (start_slot, count, requested roots) and be limited to MAX_REQUEST_BLOCKS_DENEB.
All received blocks and envelopes from sync must pass structural validation before integration into local database.
After bid validation, the bid's fee_recipient and gas_limit must exactly match the stored proposer preferences for the target slot.
After builder balance check, the builder's excess balance must be confirmed sufficient to cover the execution payment.
Bids for slots without published proposer preferences must be rejected.
Fee_recipient and gas_limit matching between bid and proposer preferences must use exact equality.
The beacon state must accurately reflect builder registration status; builders cannot manipulate their active status.
Proposer preferences must be published and propagated through gossip before builders submit bids for the corresponding slot.
An attacker cannot forge valid BLS signatures for proposer preferences or builder bids.
Before SSTORE classification, the original value (value at transaction start), current value, and new value must all be retrieved.
When current == new (no-op), SSTORE must charge exactly 200 gas.
When slot is fresh (original == current) and original is zero, SSTORE must charge 20000 gas (creating new storage).
When slot is fresh (original == current) and original is non-zero, SSTORE must charge 5000 gas (modifying existing storage).
When slot is dirty (original != current), SSTORE must charge exactly 200 gas regardless of the new value.
When a fresh non-zero slot is set to zero, 15000 must be added to the refund counter.
When a dirty slot is restored to its original value, the refund must be 19800 (if original was 0) or 4800 (if original was non-zero).
When a previously cleared slot (current=0) is set to non-zero, 15000 must be removed from the refund counter.
The final transaction refund must be capped at max(0, min(refund_counter, gas_used / 2)).
The 'original value' for a storage slot is defined as the value at transaction start and does not change within nested calls.
The refund mechanism must not allow any transaction to receive more gas back than it consumed, preventing gas-printing attacks.
Contracts using high SSTORE costs for reentrancy protection may become vulnerable under reduced gas costs; the 200-gas dirty SSTORE enables reentrancy attacks.
The block number and uncle index parameters must be validated before uncle block lookup.
The EIP-1559 fork activation block must be correctly determined for the queried chain.
For uncle blocks created before EIP-1559, the response must NOT include the baseFee field.
For uncle blocks created on or after EIP-1559, the response MUST include the baseFee field formatted as a standard Quantity hex value.
When no uncle exists at the specified index, the response must return null.
On chains without EIP-1559 activation, the baseFee field must always be omitted from uncle block responses.
The node must have accurate knowledge of the EIP-1559 fork activation block for the chain being queried.
The chainId in wallet_switchEthereumChain must be valid hexadecimal per EIP-695 format.
The target chain must exist in the wallet's chain registry and be serviceable for RPC requests.
The wallet must display the requesting dapp's identity and target chain details to the user before switching.
On user-approved switch, all pending RPC requests and chain-specific confirmations for the old chain must be cancelled before switching.
After a successful chain switch, the wallet must forward all subsequent RPC requests to the new target chain.
A rejected switch (unknown chain or user rejection) must return an appropriate error to the requesting dapp.
Wallet must apply countermeasures against fingerprinting via chain probing; automatic rejection must not reveal wallet's chain support set.
Pending RPC requests and user confirmations for the old chain must be cancelled during chain switch to prevent confusion.
The wallet must reliably identify the requesting dapp's origin to prevent impersonation attacks.
Timing attacks on chain switch rejection responses must not reveal whether a chain is supported by the wallet.
